page.layout: One printed page (left) of running text in a single column, with marginal reference numbers 2, 3, 4 and 5 in the left margin, beside the text lines. Below the column, the catchword "Jure" at the right. A narrow strip of another page's text at the right edge is the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: nium eft de futurâ in illa tribu Regia dignitatis quam ἀειφεγεσιτικῶς[?] describit pius senex, adhibi-tis in eam rem poteftatis regiæ & notiffimo infig-ni, Sceptro [Σκηπτροῦχοι βασιλῆες[?]] & potiffimâ prærogativâ, Jure Legislativo, 2. 2 Deut. 33. 4. 5. Moses eo nomine fuiffe dicitur quafi Rex in Ifrae-le, quòd congregatis principibus populi & tribubus Legem eis præceperit; 3. 3. Pfal. 60. 7. Judah Legi-ftator meus, id eft, Rex: ficque ibi vertit vulgatus interpres, Judah Rex meus. 4. 4. In Textu demum propofito, Prov. 8. 15. Per me Reges regnant, & Legum conditores justa decernunt. Ubi (quod folenne eft Salomoni in toto hoc Proverbiorum volumine, ut verfus pars posterior prioris, aut exegesin contineat, aut antithesin,) iidem ipfi, qui in priore compositis parte, Reges, in posteriore ἐξηγητικὸς Legum conditores dicuntur. 5. 5. In novo etiam Teftamento νόμως βασιλικὰς meminit Jacobus Apoftolus, Jac. 2. 8.

Confirmatur Secundò, Philosophorum, Historicorum, & Juris cùm Civilis, tum noftri Anglorum municipalis Confultorum, quæ paffim occurrunt frequentibus teftimoniis: Nos pauciffimis, ut re manifestâ, contenti erimus. Legem Principis opus effe afferunt Aristoteles, Plutarchus, aliique innumeri optimæ notæ authores. Sed imprimis celebre eft illud Ulpiani, quod in Jure Romano habetur, Quod Principi placuit Legis habet vigorem. Quod, ne ἀ[illegible, ~5 letters] & perperam intellectum tyran-nicæ dominationi viam ftruere videatur, fic olim explicuit Bractonus noftras: Quod Principi placuit; id eft, non quicquid eft à Rege temerè & ex animi perturbati impetu quodam & æstu præsumptum, fed quicquid ex Magnatum suorum consilio (Regio affensu authoritatem præstante) & habita super hoc deliberatione & tractatu (fic enim ille loquitur) rectè fuerit definitum. Quin & in

page.notes: Left margin carries only the numbers 2, 3, 4, 5, each beside a text line; they are transcribed as notes at their places. The "Jure" below the text is the catchword. The right edge strip (text beginning "Jure", "in f", "ges", etc.) belongs to the neighbouring page and is omitted. Greek words are read with doubt: "ἀειφεγεσιτικῶς" and "Σκηπτροῦχοι βασιλῆες" are uncertain; the word after "ne" is illegible. "dignitatis" is printed with a faint final letter, uncertain. "Bractonus" is uncertain; the printed form may be "Braffonus" with a long s. Possible printed errors are left as they stand.
